body: Was the ESLint configuration complaining about the structure not being created prior to usage here?
Again, do we want to allow inline types? It might be handy. I feel like creating interfaces for each step is verbose, sometimes harder to read and hard to name.
Why was the `queryID` converted to a number?

We can return the same data type.

```suggestion
                    return '';
```
Interfaces and types are useful when you repeat, but would feel over the top for me if necessary everywhere

The ESLint configuration wants us to explicitly describe the return type of the `hoganHelpers` function. I could have put it inline without creating an interface but I found it clearer that way. 

Rule: [explicit-function-return-type](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/explicit-function-return-type.md)
There is no rules that restrict the usage of inline types, so you're free to use what is best for your usage. In this specific case I just found clearer to use an interface and a type.

For what I understand it was an error since `Hit.__queryID` is typed as a `number` in [src/types/instantsearch.ts](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/src/types/instantsearch.ts#L45-L70) and `addQueryID` is returning an array of `Hit`.

```suggestion
const PoweredBy React.FC<Props> = ({ url, theme, cssClasses })  => (
```

this style seems less repetitive to me, WDYT?
This doesn't work with our Preact setup.

No opinion on this but one issue is that `eslint-plugin-react`'s `prop-types` rule does not support this pattern and will mark `url`, `theme` and `cssClasses` as missing in proptypes. 

```js
const PoweredBy: React.FC<Props> = ({ url, theme, cssClasses }: Props) => (
```
would works but it makes us repeat `Props` :neutral_face:
Let's see if @tkrugg can confirm.
This name is confusing because it implies that it's an array. Would `SuitOptions` make more sense here? (that's one drawback of naming things)
No objection to rename it (I was not convinced by the name myself :neutral_face:  )
(I should definitively add the support for this pattern in the plugin)

I tried it in the storybook and it is a string:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6137112/56643413-e45eba00-6679-11e9-92c3-05611894a229.png)

The type in `instantsearch.ts`  is therefore wrong.
Ok, I fix it the other way around then :+1:
yes `queryID` and `__queryID` should be of type string.

From what I understand on [TypeScript `void` doc](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/basic-types.html#void), `void` accepts both `undefined` and `null`. We never return `null` in `dispose()`. This change is not a big deal though.
